results.reason: A user asking 'which approach should I take, SQL or NoSQL?' fits decide's positive scope ('which approach' on any engineering decision) and architect's explicit positive scope ('SQL vs NoSQL for this workload'). Architect's exclusion only bars yes/no or which-vendor decisions without structure to design, which doesn't apply here, and decide's exclusion ('not for designing how a system is structured') is ambiguous for a technology choice vs. structure design.

Decide produces a decision brief for choosing; plan produces an executable plan with per-step specs. 'Scope and sequencing' in decide is about the decision of what to include, while plan's 'scope this refactor' is about breaking work into steps. Distinct outputs and intents.
Decide is for choosing/decision-making; build is for writing code. No overlap in positive scope.
Decide is for choosing among options; review is for reviewing code before it lands. No overlap.
Decide is for choosing among options; debug is for diagnosing failures. No overlap.
Decide is for decision-making; git-ops is for git/GitHub operations. No overlap.

Architect's positive scope includes 'monolith vs services' and 'SQL vs NoSQL,' but decide explicitly excludes 'designing how a system is structured (architect),' which covers these system-structure questions. The exclusion resolves the overlap.

Architect is system-level design; plan is code-level executable planning. Plan explicitly excludes 'system-level design (architect),' and architect excludes 'code-level planning of one change (plan).' Distinct levels.
Architect is system structure design; build is writing code. No overlap.
Architect includes 'review our architecture' (system-level); review is for reviewing code before it lands. Different review targets.
Architect is system design; debug is diagnosing failures. No overlap.
Architect is system design; git-ops is git operations. No overlap.

Plan produces an executable plan with per-step specs; decide produces a decision brief. 'Where do I start' (plan) is execution-oriented, while 'I'm stuck' (decide) is decision-oriented. Distinct outputs.
Plan is code-level executable planning and explicitly excludes 'system-level design (architect).' No overlap.
Plan produces plans and per-step specs with no code; build writes code. No overlap.
Plan is for creating executable plans; review is for reviewing code. No overlap.
Plan is for creating executable plans; debug is for diagnosing failures. Plan explicitly excludes 'diagnosing failures (debug).' No overlap.
Plan is for executable planning; git-ops is for git operations. No overlap.
Build is for writing code; decide is for choosing among options. No overlap.
Build is for writing code; architect is for system structure design. No overlap.
Build writes code; plan produces plans and specs with no code. No overlap.
Build writes code; review reviews code before it lands. No overlap.

Build fixes bugs with known causes; debug diagnoses unknown failures. Debug explicitly excludes 'fixing a bug whose cause is already known (build).' The trigger phrases differ ('fix this' vs 'why is this failing').
Build writes code; git-ops handles git operations. No overlap.
Review is for reviewing code; decide is for choosing among options. No overlap.
Review covers code-level review ('check this diff,' 'is this over-engineered'); architect covers system-level structure design ('review our architecture'). Different review targets.
Review is for reviewing code; plan is for creating executable plans. No overlap.
Review assesses code before it lands; build writes code. No overlap.
Review finds bugs during code review before landing; debug diagnoses active failures (failing tests, crashes, stack traces). Different contexts and triggers.
Review assesses code readiness ('is this ready to merge'); git-ops performs git operations ('merge'). Assessment vs. operation. No overlap.
Debug diagnoses failures; decide chooses among options. No overlap.
Debug diagnoses failures; architect designs system structure. No overlap.
Debug diagnoses failures; plan creates executable plans. No overlap.
Debug diagnoses unknown failures; build fixes bugs with known causes. Build explicitly excludes 'diagnosing an unknown failure (debug).' Distinct triggers.
Debug diagnoses active failures; review reviews code before it lands. No overlap.

Debug's positive scope includes 'CI or lint error' and 'why is this failing,' while git-ops' positive scope includes 'CI failures.' A user asking 'why is CI failing?' is clearly inside debug's positive scope and also reasonably triggers git-ops. Neither description's exclusions prevent this overlap.
Git-ops handles git operations; decide is for choosing among options. No overlap.
Git-ops handles git operations; architect designs system structure. No overlap.
Git-ops handles git operations; plan creates executable plans. No overlap.
Git-ops handles git operations; build writes code. No overlap.
Git-ops performs git operations ('merge,' 'open a PR'); review assesses code readiness ('is this ready to merge'). Operation vs. assessment. No overlap.

Git-ops' positive scope includes 'CI failures,' and debug's positive scope includes 'CI or lint error.' A user reporting a CI failure is clearly inside git-ops' positive scope and also reasonably triggers debug. Neither description's exclusions prevent this overlap.
